title: Equity and mutual fund advice
objectives: Evaluate equity funds and direct stocks for a client.
body_md:
## Direct equity or funds

Direct stocks need time and skill; **mutual funds** give diversification and professional management. For most clients, funds form the core.

## Fund selection

- **Category** fit to the goal and horizon.
- **Consistency** (rolling returns), risk-adjusted measures (Sharpe, alpha), downside capture.
- **Cost** (TER), **portfolio quality**, turnover, manager tenure and process.
- **Overlap** with existing holdings.
- Prefer **Direct plans** in advisory.

## Index funds and ETFs

Low cost and tracking error; good for the core when active funds struggle to beat the benchmark after costs.

## Valuation inputs

- **P/E, P/B, EV/EBITDA**, earnings growth and ROE.
- Compare with history and peers; valuation sets the **margin of safety**.

> **Exam tip:** Cost and consistency beat last year's return.
example: A client holds three large-cap funds with 70% of the same stocks. Adding a fourth adds little. Replace one with a mid-cap or index fund to cut overlap.
say: We pick funds on category, consistency, cost and overlap.
Past one-year return is only one data point.
never: Buy the top performer of last year.
More funds always mean more diversification.
